contract.words: I want to collect $1,000 of settled cash within 14 days. I have no money to put in up front. Find me something real.

terms.proofCondition: A paying buyer's money has settled in the owner's account

strategy.title: Upwork fixed-price writing contracts, delivered by the owner with AI assistance
strategy.why: The only route that needs $0, reaches a buyer population that posts fresh paid requests daily (about 99 new Upwork writing jobs a day; 794,000 active Upwork clients), and can settle inside 14 days (approval + Upwork's 5-day fixed-price hold). What buyers actually pay a new profile and how many proposals turn into funded contracts are unknown, so a $0 five-day test decides whether to go on.

alternatives.why: Price is only a vendor list price ($150-$750 asked, no purchase shown), close rate unknown, and Stripe's first payout waits 7-14 days after the first live payment, leaving no room inside 14 days.

alternatives.title: DataAnnotation hourly AI-training work by the owner
alternatives.why: One payer, selective acceptance and no guaranteed hours: the owner may not be approved or given 40 paid hours within 14 days; it is a job, not a population of buyers.

alternatives.why: Brain refused it: Fiverr's 14-day clearing period puts the first settled cash after day 14.

reviews.reasons: The route is sensible for a $0, 14-day goal and the plan honestly marks price and hire rate UNKNOWN, but as written it is not startable inside its own limits and its gate does not predict the target. (1) $0 cap vs Connects: every Upwork proposal costs Connects; the plan assumes 40+ proposals on 'free Connects only' with no source for how many free Connects a new profile gets (the routeSearches page is not in sources; I could not open it, 403 to WebFetch and brain_fetch_source). If the free allowance covers only a handful of proposals, the test cannot run at $0. This is research-answerable and must be established or the proposal count sized to it. (2) The ledger contradicts the continue rule and has no slack: the continue rule says 6 contracts funded by day 8 and delivered within 1-2 days so approvals land by day 9, but the cash rows approve contracts 3-6 on day 8 (settling day 13). With approvals on day 9 settlement is day 14, the last day, and day 10 means day 15, outside the window. Client approval time is the client's (fixed-price milestones can sit for days before auto-release) and withdrawal from Upwork to the owner's account, which is what the proof condition requires ('settled in the owner's account'), adds further days not modelled. (3) The proof gate does not imply the target: 2 funded from 40 proposals is a 5% hire rate, at which 6 contracts need ~120 proposals, so 80 more in 3 days, which collides with point (1). (4) validation.decides lists CONVERSION and OFFER_AND_PRICE only, but SETTLES_IN_TIME (approval + hold + withdrawal inside 14 days), ECONOMICS (Connects at $0 and the Upwork fee, '~10%' unsourced) and FULFILMENT (new-profile approval in the Writing category) are equally unestablished.
